item.title: Investors Wary After Warsh Speech Fuels Rate-Hike Bets
item.description: Some investors are voicing skepticism about mounting speculation that Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh is poised to raise interest rates. After Warsh reiterated his commitment to bringing down inflation in a highly anticipated speech on Friday, swaps traders see a rate hike as more likely than not at the central bank’s next decision in mid-September. Sarah Hunt, Chief Market Strategist at Alpine Saxon Woods, offers her equity outlook post-Jackson Hole. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Steel Rally May Be Near Its Peak: Analyst
item.description: Wells Fargo’s Equity Research Analyst Timna Tanners pours cold water on the steel rally, warning that high prices could attract imports and face pressure from new domestic capacity. She calls Canada’s looming counter-tariffs largely symbolic and explains why Nucor and Steel Dynamics could outperform if steel prices retreat. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: LG Deal Advances Arkansas Lithium Project
item.description: Standard Lithium CEO David Park joins Bloomberg Open Interest on the company's new deal with LG Energy Solutions and how it could unlock financing for a major US lithium project. He also warns China’s dominance of lithium chemicals poses a strategic threat and says booming demand from AI data centers, energy storage, EVs and defense could reshape the domestic lithium market. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Dollar Set to Weaken for a Second Month on Treasury Buyback
item.description: The dollar is on pace to fall for a second straight month as US plans to accelerate buyback of government debt weighed on the greenback.
item.dc:creator: Anya Andrianova

item.title: Bloomberg Surveillance 8/31/2026
item.description: Jonathan Ferro, Lisa Abramowicz and Annmarie Hordern speak daily with leaders and decision makers from Wall Street to Washington and beyond. No other program better positions investors and executives for the trading day. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Stocks Fall as US-Iran Strikes Spur Rally in Oil
item.description: A flare-up in geopolitical risks sent stocks and bonds lower as oil climbed, raising concerns about inflationary pressures that could make the Federal Reserve raise interest rates. Tracie McMillion, Head of Global Asset Allocation Strategy at Wells Fargo, discusses the constructive backdrop for stocks and commodities. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: SEC Tees Up Plan to Scrap Shareholder Proxy Proposal Rules
item.description: The Securities and Exchange Commission is planning to scrap rules governing how and when public company shareholders can bring proxy proposals, according to a new post by the Office of Management and Budget.
item.dc:creator: Lydia Beyoud

item.title: Ex-Congressman Santos Banned for Life by Kalshi After CFTC Case
item.description: Ex-Congressman George Santos won’t be able to place another wager on Kalshi Inc. after the prediction market platform banned him for life for allegedly manipulating wagers on his attendance at this year’s State of the Union address.
item.dc:creator: Nicola M White

item.title: How to Fix Our Broken Unemployment System
item.description:
America’s unemployment insurance system was designed for the workers of the 1920s. It was so utterly inadequate during the pandemic — the most sudden and severe job loss the US has ever seen — that Congress had to build a whole new program even as it was propping up the old one.
Now Americans are afraid of the impact AI will have on their jobs and careers, and a lack of leadership is feeding that fear. If government and elected officials want to be responsive to their constituents, they need to address this anxiety head on. The most direct way to do that is to build a new program to help workers who are looking for a job.
Bloomberg Opinion columnist and economist Kathryn Anne Edwards has a solution to our broken unemployment system. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: 'Shadow Homebuyers' Wait on Affordability Improvement
item.description: Lisa Sturtevant, Chief Economist at Bright MLS, discusses the current real estate market and how affordability pains are causing 'shadow homebuyers' to wait until rates drop in order to buy. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: PG&E Falls on Liability Bill; Nvidia Rises on Chip Investment | Stock Movers
item.description:
On this episode of Stock Movers:
- PG&E (PGE) are extending their downward move as California legislators introduced a bill that would update the state’s wildfire response without shifting liability away from publicly traded utilities. At least three research firms, including BMO Capital Markets and Wells Fargo, downgraded the stock. - Chevron (CVX) and ExxonMobil (XOM) shares are rising along with the price of oil. Washington and Tehran exchanged strikes for the first time in about a month, with US Central Command targeting rocket launchers preparing to send mines into the Strait of Hormuz. In response, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said that it had attacked US air bases in Jordan. - Nvidia (NVDA) shares are rising after the leader in AI chips dropped 4.6% Friday. It's the only stock rising in the Mag 7 on Monday. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: USDA Appeases Ranchers With Moves to Ease Beef Regulations
item.description: The US Agriculture Department is easing regulations for ranchers and small meat processors, in the latest effort to appease domestic producers while the Trump administration simultaneously boosts imports.
item.dc:creator: Ilena Peng

item.title: US Natural Gas Ticks Up on Hotter Forecasts, Cooling Demand
item.description: US natural gas futures were up slightly as near-term forecasts showed hotter weather in the coming weeks, indicating increased cooling demand for the power-plant fuel as consumers crank up air-conditioning.
item.dc:creator: Ruth Liao

item.title: Major UAE Oil Refinery Returns to Full Capacity After War Hit
item.description: Abu Dhabi National Oil Co. has restored to full capacity one of the world’s biggest oil refineries that was hit earlier in the regional war, according to people familiar with the situation.
item.dc:creator: Anthony Di Paola and Jack Farchy

item.title: S&P 500 Falls Amid Oil Spike as Middle East Conflict Intensifies
item.description: US stocks slumped on Monday, led by declines in interest-rate sensitive utilities shares while gains in energy companies offset losses elsewhere, after the US and Iran exchanged strikes for the first time in about a month.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Menton

item.title: PG&E, Edison International Stocks Plunge on California Wildfire Bill
item.description: Shares of PG&E Corp., Edison International and Sempra plunged Monday after an effort by California Governor Gavin Newsom to shift wildfire liabilities from the state’s utilities failed.
item.dc:creator: Monique Mulima and Emma Haidar

item.title: War, Weather Push Crop Prices to Biggest Monthly Gain Since 2012
item.description: Crop prices are set to cap their biggest monthly jump in more than a decade as wars and extreme weather disrupt supplies, raising concerns about food inflation.
item.dc:creator: Eleanor Thornber and Ben Westcott

item.title: Yen’s Breach of 160 Level Puts Market on Intervention Watch
item.description: The yen’s breach of 160 versus the dollar underscores the Japanese currency’s vulnerability to further weakness and the heightened risk of authorities entering the market again to slow its decline.
item.dc:creator: John Cheng

item.title: Stocks Fall as US-Iran Strikes Spur Rally in Oil: Markets Wrap
item.description: A flare-up in geopolitical risks sent stocks and bonds lower as oil climbed, raising concerns about inflationary pressures that could make the Federal Reserve raise interest rates.
item.dc:creator: Rita Nazareth

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 31
item.description: Oil rose as tensions spiked in the Middle East, with the US and Iran exchanging strikes for the first time in about a month and Tehran claiming a tanker was hit by mines in the critical Strait of Hormuz.
item.dc:creator: Paul Burkhardt, Charles Gorrivan and Mia Gindis
